messages:
maria: FYI — drafting an on-prem / VPC bring-up runbook for an air-gapped customer (ACME). Need checklist we can hand off to solutions + ops. Key constraints: no internet egress from compute, customer provides L3 network and BGP to edge router, 8x A100 nodes initial pool, private KMS required, expected go-live in 3 weeks. Draft below, please review and add missing steps.

maria: RUNBOOK DRAFT START
1) Pre-delivery
 - Confirm hardware shipping manifest + serials
 - Confirm rack/power layout and POE for remote OOB (iLO/DRAC)
 - Confirm GPU SKUs and driver compatibility (NVIDIA driver + CUDA)
 - Validate customer network CIDRs, core router contact, and firewall owners
 - Validate on-prem KMS/HSM model + network restrictions
 - Agree on maintenance window and test window

2) On-site network handshake (customer leads)
 - Ensure L2/L3 connectivity to our edge router
 - BGP peering: ASNs, prefixes, MD5 for MD5 auth if available
 - NAT rules for control-plane egress to management jumpbox (controlled egress host)
 - Ports to open: 22 (jumpbox), 443 (control-plane TLS), 2379/2380 (etcd) only between control-plane nodes, 10250 (kubelet) restricted to master subnet
 - VPN or physical cross-connect for KMS if required

3) Air-gapped bootstrap
 - Use signed artifacts bundle (tarball) delivered on encrypted USB or S3->customer import
 - Install from local registry (containerd/registry): mirror images using our registry sync tool
 - Install base OS packages from approved repo snapshot
 - Validate image signatures and checksums

4) Cluster provisioning
 - Provision control plane (3 nodes recommended), then etcd with disk encryption
 - Configure CNI with the customer CIDR and MTU tuning (jumbo frames if configured)
 - Provision GPU node pool (8 nodes) with NVIDIA driver/Device Plugin, enable MIG if requested
 - Configure node labels for dedicated tenant isolation and taints for workloads

5) Security & secrets
 - Integrate with customer KMS/HSM for sealing secrets (sealed-secrets or HSM-backed KMS)
 - Ensure control-plane TLS certs signed by customer CA or our interim CA per contract
 - Audit logging enabled and forwarded to customer SIEM collector (if provided)

6) Observability & health checks
 - Deploy lightweight Prometheus + node-exporter, nvidia-smi exporter, and a small Grafana
 - Configure alerting for GPU ECC, power supply, and temperature thresholds
 - Pre-load synthetic load test (perf synthetic) that exercises KV cache and batching

7) Validation tests (must pass before handoff)
 - k8s health: all pods in kube-system running
 - GPU test: run 3x 1-minute infer jobs on each GPU, check p99 latency < target
 - Network test: BGP failover simulation and control-plane connectivity under degraded MTU
 - KMS test: 3 roundtrip encrypt/decrypt operations using customer KMS
 - Failure test: node reboot, control-plane leader election, pod reschedule correctness

8) Cost & capacity
 - Initial commit: 8x A100 (estimate $X/mo for Dedicated equivalent) — include OPEX note for remote support sessions
 - Autoscaler policy: min=8, target=8, burst policy allowed for 2 extra nodes for 2 hrs/day

9) Handoff
 - Compile acceptance artifacts: test logs, prometheus snapshots, network captures
 - Runbook handoff meeting with recorded walkthrough and 2-week on-call overlap
 - Escalation contacts and SLOs in writing

END RUNBOOK DRAFT
